s1.syndrome_frame: lesion on the eyelid with conjunctival and eyelid abnormalities in an anophthalmic socket
salient_findings: pearly lesion on the left lower eyelid
contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue
increased scleral show of the ocular prosthesis
key_facts: patient has a history of traumatic icicle injury to the left eye
patient underwent lower eyelid reconstruction 14 years prior
patient has an anophthalmic socket with an implant
patient's ocular prosthesis would spontaneously extrude from the socket
lesion on the left lower eyelid has been growing over the past few months
patient has conjunctival shrinkage and eyelid skin contracture
biopsy revealed nodular BCC with an infiltrative pattern
no signs of fibrosis or inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: biopsy revealed nodular BCC with an infiltrative pattern

shortlist.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: lesion on the eyelid with conjunctival and eyelid abnormalities

shortlist.label: Sebaceous Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: patient has an anophthalmic socket with an implant and a growing lesion

shortlist.label: Merkel Cell Carcinoma

shortlist.label: Morpheaform Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: patient's history of traumatic injury and subsequent reconstruction

raw.rationale: The biopsy revealed nodular BCC with an infiltrative pattern, which matches the clinical presentation of a growing pearly lesion on the left lower eyelid.

rejected.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: No evidence of squamous cell carcinoma was found in the biopsy results

rejected.label: Sebaceous Carcinoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results did not indicate sebaceous carcinoma, and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest it

rejected.label: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: Merkel cell carcinoma is a rare and aggressive tumor, and the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Morpheaform Basal Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: While morpheaform basal cell carcinoma can cause cicatricial effects, the biopsy results specifically identified nodular BCC with an infiltrative pattern, making this a less likely diagnosis
